newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - Feb 27.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - Feb 27.

text.p: These are the leading stories in Manila newspapers on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The Commission on Elections (Comelec) says it is helpless to stop a signature campaign to amend the Constitution. Election registrars are therefore validating the signatures gathered by the group Pirma (Sign) because it has skirted the supreme Court's temporary restraining order. (PHILIPPINE DAILY INQUIRER)

- The Philippine government, which has struggled for more than a decade to recover some $500 million in assets of the late President Marcos, will have to wait longer. A Zurich court has upheld appeals by Marcos lawyers, Swiss banks, and other interested parties against a 1995 decision to put the money into an escrow account in the Philippines pending court action there, officials said on Tuesday. (MALAYA)

- An opposition congressman said on Wednesday that Presidential Adviser for Political Affairs Gabriel Claudio was one of the Palace officials behind the signature drive initiated by proponents of constitutional amendments. (MANILA TIMES)

- Budget Secretary Salvador Enriquez approved on Thursday the immediate release of 400 million pesos out of this year's budget to fund the nationwide barangay (village) elections to be held on May 12, 1997. (PHILIPPINE STAR)
- Government efforts to step up monitoring of tax collections, mainly from corporations, are expected to trigger a 27.5 percent increase in corporate income tax revenues this year. (INQUIRER)

- The National Statistics Office said that according to its survey of key manufacturing enterprises in December, the volume of production index dropped by 2.6 percent from the same period last year. ( MANILA TIMES)
- San Miguel Corp will put its customers' loyalty to the test next month when it raises prices by 10.5 percent to offset a greater tax bite. (TODAY)
